reviewScope: Independent technical pre-incorporation review of the unsigned R6-corrected round-two remediation candidate against the exact canonical target, accepted Gate 1 record, frozen round-two evidence, and preserved Critic records R1 through R6. The review independently verified all 47 manifest hashes, ran both validator modes, reproduced the R6 lifecycle.delete-copy exact-copy negative matrix, confirmed the R5 resource, credential-lifetime, delegation and upstream-scope closures, confirmed full R4 matrix execution, checked that the R3 technical counterexamples remain closed, and tested one-to-one lifecycle bindings across immutable request, signed authority, provider resource, inventory, receipt and tombstone. The candidate was not required to be canonical at this pre-incorporation stage.

integrityChecks.validatorReported: PASS R6 corrected candidate oracles only; next state is fresh-context preflight, not canonicalization

decision.rationale: The 47-file package is hash-consistent, both validator modes pass, all declared R6 lifecycle.delete-copy negative cases deny with typed zero effects, the R5 resource/lifetime/delegation/upstream-scope cases remain closed, the R4 matrices execute fully, and the R3 technical counterexamples remain closed. One lifecycle data-integrity blocker remains. A multi-copy disposition can reach deleted-tombstoned after one exact provider request when receipt and tombstone rows reuse that request digest for two inventory entries. Separately, raw crypto-erasure can reach deleted-tombstoned when the immutable provider request names a key identifier different from the signed inventory and policy-grant key while the receipt and tombstone claim disposition of the inventoried key. The required one-to-one binding across signed authority, exact provider request, inventory, receipt and tombstone is therefore incomplete. Zero technical blocker/major is not met, so the candidate is not ready for authorized incorporation.

newFindings.impact: Receipt and tombstone assertions can stand in for missing or differently scoped destructive provider requests. The oracle therefore does not prove that every present copy or raw erasure key was independently authorized and acted upon exactly once before lifecycle completion.
newFindings.requiredResolution: Require one signed authorization and one exact provider request per present copy or erasure key. Each request must byte-bind tenant, class, target, policy, current inventory or policy grant, copyId, provider, copy kind, object key, version and key identifier as applicable. Require a bijection between present inventory entries, signed per-copy or per-key authorities, provider-resource and CAS snapshots, immutable request digests, provider receipts and tombstone dispositions: no request digest or idempotency key may satisfy two distinct inventory entries, and no receipt or tombstone row may identify a resource different from its request. For raw crypto-erasure, bind the exact key identifier in the qualified signed policy grant or a separately signed per-key authority and compare it to the inventory and request before effect. Replace the fixed two-action lifecycle assumption with a cardinality check that executes exactly one authorized provider action for every present entry plus the final tombstone action. Add positive two-copy and multi-key cases and coherent zero-effect negatives for missing, duplicate, substituted, stale, restored and retry/race bindings. Refresh all affected hashes and repeat fresh independent pre-incorporation review.
